sources.title: California Code of Civil Procedure section 135
sources.role: Defines judicial holidays, including Saturdays and the day after Thanksgiving, and allows the Judicial Council to designate an alternate day when a judicial holiday falls on a Saturday or Sunday.

sources.title: California Government Code section 6700
sources.role: State holiday list that CCP 135 uses as the starting point for judicial holidays.

sources.title: California Rules of Court, rule 1.11
sources.role: When a CCP 135 judicial holiday falls on Saturday, courts observe the preceding Friday; when it falls on Sunday, the following Monday.

sources.title: Find Your Court | Judicial Branch of California
sources.role: Official county superior-court locator used only as a link-out. County does not change statewide holiday results.

notes: Dates in holidays[] are the observed dates published on courts.ca.gov/about/court-holidays, not dates recomputed from statute.
This dataset does not include Lunar New Year, Diwali, Genocide Remembrance Day, Admission Day, or Columbus Day, which CCP 135 excludes from judicial holidays.
Good Friday is a partial-day state holiday under Gov. Code 6700 and is not a full-day judicial holiday under CCP 135.

Saturday and Sunday are treated as closed in the checker even when they are not named rows here (CCP 135 makes every Saturday a judicial holiday; Sunday is a state holiday under Gov. Code 6700(a)(1)).

ambiguous.name: New Year's Day 2028 (observed) — not on statewide list
ambiguous.detail: January 1, 2028 is a Saturday. Some county superior-court pages list Friday, December 31, 2027 as the observed New Year's Day 2028 holiday. The statewide 2027 list on courts.ca.gov/about/court-holidays ends at Christmas Day (Friday, December 24) and does not include December 31, 2027. This dataset does not treat 2027-12-31 as a scheduled judicial holiday.
